status: Formative draft; not a validated exam

questions.title: A doorway handoff
questions.scenario: Maya brings Leo to the next room. Jordan is already supervising that room. Maya thinks Jordan has accepted Leo, but Jordan has not replied.
questions.question: What should Maya do before leaving Leo with Jordan?
options: Leave because Jordan can see the doorway.
Ask Jordan to accept care of Leo, wait for a clear reply, and check Leo against the attendance list.
Ask another child to watch Leo.
Finish the paperwork in the office first.
questions.why: An adult must clearly accept responsibility. Seeing another adult nearby does not prove the handoff is complete.
questions.example: It is like handing someone a full cup: make sure they have hold of it before you let go.
questions.task: Practice a handoff with a partner. Name the child, receive a reply, and check the attendance list.
questions.zh: Maya把Leo带到隔壁教室。离开前，她应请Jordan明确接手，等对方回应，再按当日名单核对Leo。附近有成人，不代表已经完成照护交接。
questions.critical: Leaving a child without an adult who has accepted care.

questions.title: A toy in an infant's sleep space
questions.scenario: During a routine check, you see a stuffed toy in an infant's sleep space. The infant is breathing normally and has no signs of distress. A parent says the toy helps at home.
questions.question: Which is the safest general teaching response?
options: Keep the toy because the parent requested it.
Cover the toy with a blanket.
Remove the toy, maintain supervision, and explain the safe-sleep procedure to the parent.
Wait for the next staff meeting before acting.
questions.why: A parent's familiar routine does not establish that an item is safe in an infant's sleep space. The final lesson needs current safe-sleep guidance and the applicable state rule.
questions.example: A toy can be suitable for awake, supervised play without belonging in the sleep space.
questions.task: Use an empty demonstration sleep space to identify items that need checking against current guidance. Do not use a child for the demonstration.
questions.zh: 例子中的婴儿没有紧急不适表现。先移走睡眠区域内的毛绒玩具，继续照看婴儿，再向家长解释安全睡眠做法。家中习惯不能代替安全要求。最终教材须核实现行睡眠指导与州规则。
questions.critical: Keeping a known potential sleep hazard only because of parent preference.

questions.title: Was the medicine already given?
questions.scenario: A child's medicine record is blank. One worker thinks a scheduled dose may already have been given. The child has no urgent symptoms in this example.
questions.question: What should the next worker do?
options: Give another dose so the record will be complete.
Guess from the amount left in the bottle.
Ask a child whether the medicine was given.
Do not repeat the dose on a guess; keep the child supervised and use the medication plan's qualified clinical advice route.
questions.why: A blank entry does not prove no medicine was given. The person reviewing the record must not invent a dosing decision.
questions.example: An unchecked delivery box does not prove a package never arrived; first find reliable information. Medicine decisions also need qualified clinical advice.
questions.task: Using a fictional record, identify what is known, what is uncertain, whom the plan tells you to contact, and how to record the actual advice and action.
questions.zh: 空白给药记录不等于没有给过药。不要猜测后再给一次。继续照看儿童，按用药计划联系具备资质的医疗指导人员，并如实记录。若出现紧急症状，应立即采用相应急救流程。
questions.critical: Giving a possible duplicate dose without appropriate direction.

questions.title: A child tells you something worrying
questions.scenario: During play, a child says, “Someone hurt me last night.” No immediate medical emergency is apparent. You are the caregiver receiving the statement.
questions.question: Which response best supports safety and a proper reporting process?
options: Listen calmly, avoid leading questions, record the child's own words, and follow the applicable reporting duty without waiting to prove the allegation.
Promise you will keep it secret.
Interview the other children until the story is proven.
Wait for the owner's permission before deciding whether a legally required report may be made.
questions.why: The caregiver's role is to support the child and follow reporting duties, not investigate the allegation. The jurisdiction-specific reporting trigger, recipient, and timing still need primary-source verification.
questions.example: Write “Someone hurt me last night,” rather than changing it to your own conclusion about who did what.
questions.task: Locate the applicable official reporting instructions. Identify the reporting trigger, recipient, deadline, and whether any additional written follow-up is required.
questions.zh: 平静倾听，不承诺保密，不用诱导问题追问，也不自行调查。记录儿童原话，依法履行报告义务；不为收集证据或等待老板许可而拖延已经触发的报告。报告门槛、对象和时限须按所在州核实。
questions.critical: Delaying an already-required report to obtain proof or internal approval.

questions.title: The unlabeled snack
questions.scenario: A child has a documented food-allergy plan. A visitor brings cookies with no ingredient information. A suitable snack that has already been checked against the plan is available.
questions.question: What should you offer the child?
options: The cookie after removing visible nuts.
The checked alternative, while keeping the uncertain cookies away from the child's food.
A small bite of the cookie as a test.
The cookie if another child ate one safely.
questions.why: The ingredients and cross-contact risk are unknown. Other children's reactions and removing visible pieces do not establish that this food fits the child's plan.
questions.example: A label missing from a container means you cannot tell what is inside by looking at the lid.
questions.task: Practice checking a fictional snack label against a fictional allergy plan. For emergency symptoms, use the child's emergency plan rather than this routine snack exercise.
questions.zh: 按该儿童的过敏计划提供已经核实的替代点心，不试吃，不靠挑掉可见坚果来判断安全。其他儿童吃后没事，也不能证明这个儿童可以吃。
questions.critical: Using a taste test to determine whether a child's allergen is present.

questions.title: Can one more child attend?
questions.scenario: A family requests an extra day. You have not yet checked the children's ages, attendance, qualified staff, or the current license conditions.
questions.question: Can you determine from these facts that the extra attendance is permitted?
options: Yes, because only one child is being added.
Yes, because a parent agrees to the arrangement.
No. Obtain the relevant facts and apply the current rules and license conditions before confirming attendance.
No program may ever accept an extra day.
questions.why: Neither permission nor a universal refusal follows from the facts given. A legal calculation needs the applicable rule and the actual age and staffing information.
questions.example: A room with an empty chair may still lack a qualified adult or permitted capacity.
questions.task: Use a verified rule excerpt for a specified license category, then calculate the result for a fully stated group. Do not use invented limits as state law.
questions.zh: 仅凭“多一个孩子”无法判断是否允许。先查实际年龄组合、出勤、合格人员和许可条件，再按现行规则判断。空椅子不等于有合法名额。
questions.critical: Promising admission before checking an applicable legal capacity limit.

questions.title: A request for a different tool
questions.scenario: A child has difficulty holding the thin handle used in a painting activity. The family asks whether a larger handle could be used. No individualized review has occurred.
questions.question: What should the educator do next?
options: Reject the request because every child must use identical tools.
Exclude the child from painting.
Tell the family that every request is automatically required, regardless of the facts.
Discuss the child's access needs and consider a workable change that lets the child take part.
questions.why: Individual review is more useful than a blanket refusal or an automatic promise. Exact legal duties depend on the covered program and applicable law.
questions.example: A larger handle may let the child explore the same colors and make choices alongside peers.
questions.task: Name the learning goal and propose two accessible ways to take part. Review legal applicability separately.
questions.zh: 先了解儿童的实际需要，再考虑可行调整，例如更粗的画笔手柄。目标是让儿童参与同样有意义的学习，不是一概拒绝，也不是未经分析承诺所有要求都必须满足。
questions.critical: A blanket disability-based refusal without an individualized review.

questions.title: Payment for an absence
questions.scenario: A provider in another program says every absence is payable. Your own program's current payment terms have not been checked.
questions.question: What information should guide your claim?
options: Your program's current authorization, effective payment terms, and applicable absence rules.
The other provider's experience alone.
A guessed attendance entry that matches the payment requested.
A rule that no absence can ever be paid in any program.
questions.why: Payment rules depend on the program. An absence does not by itself establish whether payment is permitted, and records must remain accurate.
questions.example: Two families can use different benefit programs with different payment arrangements even at the same child-care site.
questions.task: Using fictional records and verified program instructions, distinguish attendance facts from payment eligibility and explain a correction route.
questions.zh: 按本项目现行授权、付款条款和缺勤规则判断，不能照搬其他项目经验。出勤事实和可付款条件是不同问题，不能为了账单改造出勤记录。
questions.critical: Inventing attendance to support a payment claim.

questions.title: From toileting help to lunch
questions.scenario: A caregiver finishes helping a child use the toilet and is about to prepare food. Safe supervision is in place while the caregiver completes hygiene steps.
questions.question: What should happen before food preparation?
options: Skip hand hygiene if gloves were worn.
Complete the required handwashing steps and use clean food-handling equipment.
Wipe hands on clothing.
Only check whether the hands look dirty.
questions.why: Gloves and visible cleanliness do not replace proper hand hygiene. The final lesson should show the current handwashing procedure and applicable facility rules.
questions.example: A hand can look clean after touching a bathroom door and still need washing before making a sandwich.
questions.task: Demonstrate the verified handwashing sequence at a training sink and explain how group supervision is maintained.
questions.zh: 如厕协助后，先按正确步骤洗手，再处理食物。戴过手套、手看起来干净，都不能代替手部卫生。最终教材应配上经核实的操作步骤。
questions.critical: Skipping required hand hygiene before food handling.

questions.title: Describe what happened
questions.scenario: A worker writes, “Ava was bad again.” The worker saw Ava push a block toward Sam after Sam took a truck.
questions.question: Which note is most useful for planning support?
options: Ava is a difficult child.
Ava always behaves badly.
Ava pushed a block toward Sam after Sam took the truck; the adult moved closer and helped them take turns.
Delete the event so the family will not worry.
questions.why: A concrete observation shows the event, context, and adult response without turning a behavior into a label about the child.
questions.example: “Spilled the water while reaching for the cup” tells you more than “careless.”
questions.task: Rewrite two fictional judgmental notes as observable events. Add one developmentally appropriate support to try and observe.
questions.zh: 用可观察事实代替“坏”“难管”等标签：谁做了什么、之前发生了什么、成人怎样回应。记录的目的是帮助理解和支持儿童，不是给儿童定性。
questions.critical: No automatic safety-critical failure for wording alone; give specific feedback.

questions.title: The vehicle is quiet
questions.scenario: Children have left a program vehicle at the destination. The assigned physical vehicle check has not been completed. No child is known to be missing in this example.
questions.question: What should the responsible adult do?
options: Assume the vehicle is empty because it is quiet.
Sign the checklist from memory tomorrow.
Ask a child whether anyone stayed behind and stop there.
Complete the physical vehicle check and the transport plan's other verification steps, while maintaining supervision of the children outside.
questions.why: Silence is not a reliable check for a child left in a vehicle. A physical check and the applicable safeguards address a risk that a head count alone may miss.
questions.example: A sleeping child may not answer when someone calls into the vehicle.
questions.task: Using an empty parked training vehicle, demonstrate the approved check. A missing child or medical emergency requires the emergency procedure immediately.
questions.zh: 车辆安静不能证明车内没有儿童。按运输计划逐处实查，并完成所要求的其他核实步骤；车外儿童也必须有人照看。若儿童失踪或有紧急危险，应立即启动相应应急流程。
questions.critical: Declaring the vehicle empty without completing the assigned check.

questions.title: Respond without shaming
questions.scenario: During block play, an adult proposes making a child stand in front of the group while everyone says the child is naughty.
questions.question: What is the best response?
options: Stop the humiliating approach and guide the child toward a safe action with calm adult support.
Use the shaming activity if it works quickly.
Ask the other children to decide the punishment.
Ignore any risk because guidance must never include adult limits.
questions.why: Children need safe limits and support. Public shaming does not teach the next safe action and can harm the child's dignity.
questions.example: Say, “Blocks stay on the floor. I can help you build here,” while moving close enough to support safe play.
questions.task: Practice one brief, respectful limit and one supported alternative suited to the child's age and communication needs.
questions.zh: 停止羞辱做法，用平静、具体的话说明安全界限，并帮助儿童练习下一步。例如：“积木留在地上，我陪你在这里搭。”尊重儿童不等于放弃安全界限。
